newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - PATRIOTS HOPE TO USE UNDERDOG STATUS TO ADVANTAGE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - PATRIOTS HOPE TO USE UNDERDOG STATUS TO ADVANTAGE.

text.p: The New England Patriots are heavy underdogs going into the Super Bowl against the Green Bay Packers, but the American Football Conference champions hope to use that to their advantage.
New England middle linebacker Ted Strickland warned against discounting the Pats, rated two-touchdown underdogs by Las Vegas bookmakers for the January 26 clash in New Orleans.
"I think we thrive on all that to be honest with you," says Strickland. "We always seem to be thriving on adversity. Hey, that's the way it's going to be and we'll use that to our advantage."

Defensive lineman Pio Sagapolutele said the Pats' defence should have made believers of those who thought New England would sink or swim with its high-powered offence. The Patriots have not allowed a touchdown in the playoffs and have put immense pressure on opposition quarterbacks.
"I think there's enough proof now that we're for real," he said.
Patriots coach Bill Parcells, who twice led the New York Giants to Super Bowl triumphs, is trying to keep his young team focused on the challenge.

"He just said 'Don't worry about all the other stuff you can't control. Just worry about the game. Don't be influenced by all the hype, just concentrate on winning the football game,'" Strickland said.
Parcells, in the last year of his contract and rumoured to be considering leaving for more control with another NFL club, is right where he wants to be at this time of year.
At a press conference earlier this week, Parcells waxed nostalgic about his Super Bowl trips to Pasadena in 1987 and Tampa in 1991 with the Giants.
"There's no feeling like standing in that tunnel at the Super Bowl. When you're getting ready to come out there, there's nothing like it," he said.
Parcells said he remembers everything about those precious moments.
"I can see Pasadena like it was yesterday. I can see Tampa Stadium. I remember everything. It's so vivid. I'm telling you there's no feeling like it."
